:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
To plot $y = -\dfrac{2}{x-1}-1,$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=-\dfrac{1}{x}.$

![](images/9d/9da0db2e6c97e507e82b7ca801e46802fabf91ad31ff53ad3cc9ae580151370a.png)

- Translate it by one unit to the right to get the graph of $y=-\dfrac{1}{x-1}.$ 

![](images/8c/8ce8c53f202f04b3b34a247b797f65f7616e8772afa1751de126ddd401417bd7.png)

Notice that the vertical asymptote is now $x=1.$

- Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\dfrac{2}{x-1}.$

![](images/c9/c9b708a20d9c6c12f0016279e8d7a3ea55597e7645f0a9518f1c32e8a8406e47.png)

- Finally, translate it by $1$ unit down to get the graph of $y=-\dfrac{2}{x-1}-1.$ 

![](images/e1/e100b552adb71cae1295492a58b0e60525813adb87d9815ba64a151a856f0c46.png)

Notice that the horizontal asymptote is now $y=-1.$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
![](images/fb/fb46d056a8d8010eca509543c231c875f4980a21f1af17505fa98c8c64106207.png)

The diagram above shows the graph of $y = \dfrac{a}{x-b}+k.$ What is the value of $a+b+k?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=-1,$ while the vertical asymptote is $x=2.$ This means that $k=-1$ and $b=2,$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y = \dfrac{a}{x-2}+(-1) = \dfrac{a}{x-2}-1.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(3,2)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x-2}-1 \\ 2 & =\frac{a}{3-2}-1 \\ 3 & =\frac{a}{1} \\ a & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a+b+k = 3+2+(-1) = 4.$

- Take the curve $y=\dfrac{1}{x}.$

![](images/e8/e80865b0f32a5473da27b39537034bcdabee0a6c24032f41413e20518642d3f4.png)

- Stretch the result by a scale factor of $\dfrac{7}{2}$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=\dfrac{7}{2x}.$

![](images/b7/b7b1fe93de798c0aa91f60f66a2507869dbe837b843b7233972e1a78ee22576a.png)

To plot $y = -\dfrac{1}{5x},$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=-\dfrac{1}{x}.$

![](images/d5/d5d93e12275c683e0a56f0ec9a0c99540a7774879cd0f8fa69151ddba68a44fa.png)

- Stretch the result by a scale factor of $\dfrac 1 5$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\dfrac{1}{5x}.$

![](images/30/30ace3126ec127b9949ebf599d615020b9770458825d22460e9e7e0b3d5efec3.png)
